review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

2:1.sourceText: ἔκρινα δὲ ἐμαυτῷ τοῦτο, τὸ μὴ πάλιν ἐν λύπῃ πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐλθεῖν.
2:1.targetText: So I made up my mind not to make another painful visit to you.

groups.note: ἔκρινα ἐμαυτῷ ("I decided for myself") is rendered I made up my mind.
BSB's Greek text has a different connective here.
The articular infinitive τὸ … ἐλθεῖν ("to come") is rendered to make … visit.
πάλιν ("again") is rendered another.
ἐν λύπῃ ("in sorrow") is rendered painful.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render τοῦτο ("this"), which points ahead to the infinitive.

2:2.sourceText: εἰ γὰρ ἐγὼ λυπῶ ὑμᾶς, καὶ τίς ὁ εὐφραίνων με εἰ μὴ ὁ λυπούμενος ἐξ ἐμοῦ;
2:2.targetText: For if I grieve you, who is left to cheer me but those whom I have grieved?

groups.note: The article with the participle, "the one who cheers", is rendered to cheer.
εἰ μή ("except") is rendered but.
The singular ὁ λυπούμενος ("the one being grieved") is rendered those whom … have grieved.
ἐξ ἐμοῦ ("by me") becomes the subject of the active have grieved.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render καί ("then") at the start of the question.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula and left; the Greek has τίς ὁ εὐφραίνων ("who is the one cheering").

2:3.sourceText: καὶ ἔγραψα τοῦτο αὐτὸ ἵνα μὴ ἐλθὼν λύπην σχῶ ἀφ’ ὧν ἔδει με χαίρειν, πεποιθὼς ἐπὶ πάντας ὑμᾶς ὅτι ἡ ἐμὴ χαρὰ πάντων ὑμῶν ἐστιν.
2:3.targetText: I wrote as I did so that on my arrival I would not be saddened by those who ought to make me rejoice. I had confidence in all of you, that you would share my joy.

groups.note: τοῦτο αὐτό ("this very thing") is rendered as I did.
The participle ἐλθών ("having come") is rendered on … arrival.
λύπην σχῶ ("I might have sorrow") is rendered I would … be saddened.
ἀφ’ ("from") is rendered by.
ἐστιν with the genitive ὑμῶν ("is of you") is rendered you would share.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render καί ("and") at the start of the sentence.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB does not render πάντων ("all") here.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a possessive; the participle ἐλθών has no person.
English supplies a causative verb; in the Greek it is I who ought to rejoice (ἔδει με χαίρειν).
English supplies a subject; πεποιθώς ("being confident") is a participle.

2:4.sourceText: ἐκ γὰρ πολλῆς θλίψεως καὶ συνοχῆς καρδίας ἔγραψα ὑμῖν διὰ πολλῶν δακρύων, οὐχ ἵνα λυπηθῆτε, ἀλλὰ τὴν ἀγάπην ἵνα γνῶτε ἣν ἔχω περισσοτέρως εἰς ὑμᾶς.
2:4.targetText: For through many tears I wrote you out of great distress and anguish of heart, not to grieve you but to let you know how much I love you.

groups.note: The passive λυπηθῆτε ("you might be grieved") is rendered actively.
τὴν ἀγάπην … ἣν ἔχω ("the love that I have") is rendered I love.
περισσοτέρως ("more abundantly") is rendered how much.
εἰς ὑμᾶς ("toward you") becomes the object of love.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:5.sourceText: Εἰ δέ τις λελύπηκεν, οὐκ ἐμὲ λελύπηκεν, ἀλλὰ ἀπὸ μέρους, ἵνα μὴ ἐπιβαρῶ, πάντας ὑμᾶς.
2:5.targetText: Now if anyone has caused grief, he has not grieved me but all of you—to some degree, not to overstate it.

groups.note: ἀπὸ μέρους ("in part") is rendered to some degree.
ἐπιβαρῶ ("I may be too severe") is rendered overstate.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object; the Greek verb has none.

2:6.sourceText: ἱκανὸν τῷ τοιούτῳ ἡ ἐπιτιμία αὕτη ἡ ὑπὸ τῶν πλειόνων,
2:6.targetText: The punishment imposed on him by the majority is sufficient for him.

groups.note: τοιούτῳ ("such a one") is rendered him.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB renders ἡ ἐπιτιμία αὕτη ("this punishment") as The punishment.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a participle phrase; the Greek has only the repeated article before ὑπό ("by").
English supplies a copula; the Greek clause has no verb.

2:7.sourceText: ὥστε τοὐναντίον μᾶλλον ὑμᾶς χαρίσασθαι καὶ παρακαλέσαι, μή πως τῇ περισσοτέρᾳ λύπῃ καταποθῇ ὁ τοιοῦτος.
2:7.targetText: So instead, you ought to forgive and comfort him, so that he will not be overwhelmed by excessive sorrow.

groups.note: τοὐναντίον μᾶλλον ("on the contrary, rather") is rendered instead.
μή πως ("lest somehow") is rendered so that … not.
τοιοῦτος ("such a one") is rendered he.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a modal; ὥστε with the infinitive states the consequence.
English supplies the object; the Greek verbs have none.

2:8.sourceText: διὸ παρακαλῶ ὑμᾶς κυρῶσαι εἰς αὐτὸν ἀγάπην·
2:8.targetText: Therefore I urge you to reaffirm your love for him.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a possessive; the Greek has only ἀγάπην ("love").

2:9.sourceText: εἰς τοῦτο γὰρ καὶ ἔγραψα, ἵνα γνῶ τὴν δοκιμὴν ὑμῶν, εἰ εἰς πάντα ὑπήκοοί ἐστε.
2:9.targetText: My purpose in writing you was to see if you would stand the test and be obedient in everything.

groups.note: εἰς τοῦτο ("for this") is rendered purpose.
The finite ἔγραψα ("I wrote") is rendered My … writing.
ἵνα ("in order that") is rendered with the infinitive to.
γνῶ ("I might know") is rendered see.
τὴν δοκιμήν ("the proof") is rendered stand the test.
ὑμῶν ("your") becomes the subject you.
ἐστε ("you are") is rendered would … be.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render γάρ ("for").
BSB does not render καί ("also").

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a preposition for the gerund writing.
English supplies an object; the Greek has no ὑμῖν here.
English supplies a copula.
English joins the two parts; the Greek has no καί here.

2:10.sourceText: ᾧ δέ τι χαρίζεσθε, κἀγώ· καὶ γὰρ ἐγὼ ὃ κεχάρισμαι, εἴ τι κεχάρισμαι, δι’ ὑμᾶς ἐν προσώπῳ Χριστοῦ,
2:10.targetText: If you forgive anyone, I also forgive him. And if I have forgiven anything, I have forgiven it in the presence of Christ for your sake,

groups.note: The general relative ᾧ ("to whomever") is rendered If … anyone.
χαρίζεσθε ("you forgive") is understood again with κἀγώ.
κἀγώ ("and I") is rendered I also.
The relative ὅ ("what") is rendered it.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render δέ ("now").
BSB does not render τι ("anything") in this clause.
BSB renders καὶ γάρ ("for indeed") with And alone.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object; the Greek leaves it understood.

2:11.sourceText: ἵνα μὴ πλεονεκτηθῶμεν ὑπὸ τοῦ Σατανᾶ· οὐ γὰρ αὐτοῦ τὰ νοήματα ἀγνοοῦμεν.
2:11.targetText: in order that Satan should not outwit us. For we are not unaware of his schemes.

groups.note: The passive πλεονεκτηθῶμεν ("we might be outwitted") is rendered actively.
ὑπὸ … Σατανᾶ ("by Satan") becomes the subject of the active verb.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

2:12.sourceText: Ἐλθὼν δὲ εἰς τὴν Τρῳάδα εἰς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ Χριστοῦ, καὶ θύρας μοι ἀνεῳγμένης ἐν Κυρίῳ,
2:12.targetText: Now when I went to Troas to preach the gospel of Christ and a door stood open for me in the Lord,

groups.note: εἰς ("for") is rendered to.
The genitive absolute θύρας … ἀνεῳγμένης ("a door having been opened") is rendered a door stood open.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject; Ἐλθών ("having come") is a participle.
English supplies a verb; the Greek says εἰς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον ("for the gospel").

2:13.sourceText: οὐκ ἔσχηκα ἄνεσιν τῷ πνεύματί μου τῷ μὴ εὑρεῖν με Τίτον τὸν ἀδελφόν μου, ἀλλὰ ἀποταξάμενος αὐτοῖς ἐξῆλθον εἰς Μακεδονίαν.
2:13.targetText: I had no peace in my spirit, because I did not find my brother Titus there. So I said goodbye to them and went on to Macedonia.

groups.note: The dative articular infinitive τῷ … εὑρεῖν ("by not finding") is rendered because … did … find.
ἀλλά ("but") is rendered So.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds there, referring back to Troas.
English joins the participle clause (said goodbye) to the main verb went on.

2:14.sourceText: Τῷ δὲ Θεῷ χάρις τῷ πάντοτε θριαμβεύοντι ἡμᾶς ἐν τῷ Χριστῷ καὶ τὴν ὀσμὴν τῆς γνώσεως αὐτοῦ φανεροῦντι δι’ ἡμῶν ἐν παντὶ τόπῳ·
2:14.targetText: But thanks be to God, who always leads us triumphantly as captives in Christ and through us spreads everywhere the fragrance of the knowledge of Him.

groups.note: φανεροῦντι ("making known") is rendered spreads.
ἐν παντὶ τόπῳ ("in every place") is rendered everywhere.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the verb of the exclamation.

2:15.sourceText: ὅτι Χριστοῦ εὐωδία ἐσμὲν τῷ Θεῷ ἐν τοῖς σωζομένοις καὶ ἐν τοῖς ἀπολλυμένοις,
2:15.targetText: For we are to God the sweet aroma of Christ among those who are being saved and those who are perishing.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB lets among serve both groups, so the second ἐν has no English word.

2:16.sourceText: οἷς μὲν ὀσμὴ ἐκ θανάτου εἰς θάνατον, οἷς δὲ ὀσμὴ ἐκ ζωῆς εἰς ζωήν. καὶ πρὸς ταῦτα τίς ἱκανός;
2:16.targetText: To the one, we are an odor of death and demise; to the other, a fragrance that brings life. And who is qualified for such a task?

groups.note: οἷς μέν … οἷς δέ ("to some … to others") is rendered To the one … to the other.
ἐκ θανάτου εἰς θάνατον ("from death to death") is rendered of death and demise.
ἐκ ζωῆς εἰς ζωήν ("from life to life") is rendered brings life.
ταῦτα ("these things") is rendered such a task.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject and copula; the Greek clause has no verb.
English supplies a relative frame for the phrase ἐκ ζωῆς εἰς ζωήν.
English supplies a copula; the Greek question has no verb.

2:17.sourceText: οὐ γάρ ἐσμεν ὡς οἱ πολλοὶ καπηλεύοντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἀλλ’ ὡς ἐξ εἰλικρινίας, ἀλλ’ ὡς ἐκ Θεοῦ κατέναντι Θεοῦ ἐν Χριστῷ λαλοῦμεν.
2:17.targetText: For we are not like so many others, who peddle the word of God for profit. On the contrary, in Christ we speak before God with sincerity, as men sent from God.

groups.note: πολλοί ("many") is rendered so many others.
ἐξ ("out of") is rendered with.
Same word, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB does not render this ὡς ("as").
BSB does not render the second ἀλλά ("but").

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a noun and verb; the Greek has only ὡς ἐκ Θεοῦ ("as from God").
